title: Consent to personal jurisdiction
summary: Consent supplies a basis for personal jurisdiction through an agreement, conduct in litigation, or another legally recognized submission to the court’s authority. The assigned cases examine both how consent arises and its limits.
notes: Mallory resolves the due-process issue under the Pennsylvania registration scheme before the Court. Its separate opinions and reserved Commerce Clause issue prevent describing it as approval of every registration regime on every constitutional ground.

sections.Meaning: Consent supplies a basis for personal jurisdiction through an agreement, conduct in litigation, or another legally recognized submission to the court’s authority. The assigned cases examine both how consent arises and its limits.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the actual basis asserted: a forum clause, appearance, failure to preserve an objection, a discovery sanction, or an explicit registration statute. Apply the doctrine specific to that setting rather than treating all forms of consent as interchangeable.
